data.narrative:
Proteus Space is a Series A aerospace company founded by David Kervin (CEO, 20+ years in US military contracting) and Andrew Shapiro (CTO, 20 years at NASA JPL, led 3D-printing technology for Mars Perseverance). The company has raised $14.4M to date. The comparable universe consists of 5 public Space & Aerospace names (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) trading at a median 27.4x price-to-sales, plus 8 private peers in the same sector at adjacent stages, including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs.

Two valuation methods apply to Proteus Space. Stage-progression analysis uses the $17M total-raised proxy as a base, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A-to-next-stage progression, yielding $34M. Peer-median anchoring across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Cowboy Space at $2.0B Series B, Aalyria at $1.3B Series B, Starcloud at $1.1B Seed) produces a $1.3B median with a range of $1.1B–$2.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied; target revenue is not disclosed.

The triangulated analysis spans $29M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $667M. The wide range reflects tension between stage-based methods anchored to capital deployed and peer multiples that incorporate later-stage, larger peer valuations. Key uncertainties include revenue traction, contract pipeline specificity, and the representativeness of peer multiples given Proteus's earlier-stage position relative to Series B comparables.
